editedExercise.name: Extended-Exhale Breathing

instructions.description: Settle into a comfortable seated or lying position. Relax your shoulders, jaw, and neck, and allow your body to rest naturally.
Inhale gently and comfortably through your nose, allowing your abdomen and lower ribs to expand naturally.
Exhale slowly and smoothly through your nose or mouth, making the exhalation slightly longer than the inhalation. Keep the breath relaxed and avoid straining or holding it.
Continue for several comfortable breaths. If you feel light-headed, dizzy, or uncomfortable, stop the exercise and return to your natural breathing pattern.

performanceMetrics.notes: Record the time performed with comfortable, controlled technique.
Record a comfortable breathing rate without prescribing a universal norm.

variationSuggestions.variationDescription: Use a shorter comfortable practice period while preserving relaxed breathing.

commentsNotes: Keep the breathing gentle and comfortable rather than taking very deep breaths.
Aim for a slightly longer exhalation, not a forced or prolonged one.
Keep your shoulders and upper chest relaxed.
Maintain a smooth transition between inhaling and exhaling.
There is no need to count exact seconds; choose a rhythm that feels natural.
